question: Should OpenClaw accept the full one-Claw-one-new-agent v1 package and lifecycle contract, or narrow it before this RFC leaves draft status?
rationale: Document review can establish coherence, but it cannot authorize durable CLI, manifest, ownership, registry, provenance, update, and removal guarantees across OpenClaw and ClawHub.

options.title: Accept full v1
options.body: Approve the current contract, create or confirm the implementation tracking issue, transition the RFC to accepted, and coordinate landing of the gated implementation stack.

options.title: Narrow initial v1
options.body: Accept the core add and ownership model while deferring selected update, export, MCP, cron, or automatic cleanup guarantees to follow-up RFCs.

options.title: Continue incubation
options.body: Keep the RFC in draft and the CLI gated while implementation experience resolves remaining compatibility and operational questions.

recommendation.title: Accept full v1
recommendation.body: Approve the current contract, create or confirm the implementation tracking issue, transition the RFC to accepted, and coordinate landing of the gated implementation stack.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete product model adopted by the current branch and are the strongest visible discussion-based owner for this contract decision.
